newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - sluggish ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - sluggish ahead of holiday.

text.p: The New York physical market was thinly traded this week, with few prompt sales ahead of the three-day Easter weekend, traders said.
Also putting a damper on spot activity was a sharp rebound in futures prices this week and the CSCE May contract's widening premium to second-month July.
"The roasters are not going to chase this market up," one trader said. "There was price-fixing, but many roasters are well covered into the summer."
With roasters' needs fairly well met through the spring and the peak roasting period coming to close, traders expected business to remain sluggish.

Traders said weakening differentials on spot Colombian beans failed to tempt buyers, who still viewed the beans as unattractively expensive. Colombian MAMs for spot delivery were heard at a still hefty 34 to 38 cents over the CSCE May contract, down from about 40 cents over last week.
For later delivery, by comparison, Colombian MAMs for April shipment were offered at 24 cents over May.
